newsitem.title: GERMANY: BOXING-AIBA REBUFFS MEDITERRANEAN GAMES ORGANISERS.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-AIBA REBUFFS MEDITERRANEAN GAMES ORGANISERS.

text.p: The world amateur boxing body AIBA has rebuked the organisers of last month's Mediterranean Games for stripping an Italian of a gold medal after a computer scoring controversy.

AIBA said in its July newsletter that the original verdict giving a 3-2 victory to heavyweight Giacobbe Fragomeni must stand despite the Games' organisers overturning it in favour of Algerian Mohammed Benguesmia.

Algeria had protested after the bout in the southern Italian town of Bari and the Games' International Committee subsequently ruled that there had been a "flagrant malfunction of the computerised result."
Benguesmia was then awarded the gold and Fragomeni the silver medal.
That decision was the first time that the high-tech electronic scoring used at Olympics and world championships had been overruled.

AIBA said that the Games authorities had "no correct understanding of the way bouts are being scored by means of the computerised scoring system, and hence took a decision which contradicts the rules of AIBA."

The computerised scoring method, introduced at Olympic level in 1992 in Barcelona, involves five judges who sit around the ring scoring with coloured electronic buttons and has caused several controversies.

AIBA also said in its newsletter that its executive committee had discussed "at length" reducing the number of boxers competing in the 2000 Sydney Olympics as requested by the International Olympic Committee.

A recommendation from AIBA's Technical and Rules commission to drop two weight categories had been turned down on health grounds, apparently amid concern that boxers might be tempted to put on or lose excessive weight to make the nearest category.
